desc:
This steep and narrow ravine leads off into the distance to the south. Here, the
two walls meet, and the ravine comes to an end. There is a breach in the western
wall of the ravine, where something punched through from the other side. A
rough, uneven hole near the corner where the ravine ends leads deeper into
whatever may be found below.
name: Underground Ravine by a Breach

desc:
This hole is located in the floor of an underground ravine. The stony ground of
the ravine above is gradually replaced by dirt towards the bottom, the shift in
the geology easily evident on the hole's walls. A tunnel through the soft earth
leads off towards the south, sloping slightly downwards further toward the roots
of the world.
name: Dank Hole

desc:
An unfinished tunnel leading in from the north comes to its conclusion here. The
excavation seems to have caused a cave-in as the southern part of the tunnel
comes to an abrupt end in a jagged hole that leads down into a deeper,
natural-looking cavern. Piles of rock are heaped against the walls, the effort
to remove them apparently abandoned.
name: Unfinished Troll Burrow

desc:
A crude, unfinished tunnel has been dug through the dark bedrock here. The walls
are uneven and edges of large boulders of harder rock jut out into the tunnel.
The effort of removing them was obviously not worth the bother. Rubble is strewn
about the tunnel and the floor is covered by a deep layer of dust and grime.
name: Unfinished Troll Burrow

desc:
A burrow has been created through the hard bedrock. Great brutal force must have
been used in the effort to create this tunnel. The walls and floor show no sign
of chiseling and minecraft. Rather, the stone has been forced to give way before
raw power with great furrows and raw wounds giving witness to the impressive
effort applied to creating this tunnel.
name: Unfinished Troll Burrow

desc:
This crudely dug-out burrow, twelve or thirteen feet in diameter, lies abandoned
and dust-covered in the depths of the mountain. Quickly-rigged wooden poles and
planks secured by old, thick ropes prevents the whole area from caving in. The
soil is dark and wet, and the air is thick and heavy. To the north, there is a
massive, black troll-door resting on five massive, rusted iron hinges. The
burrow itself continues to the south.
name: Unfinished Troll Burrow

desc:
This rounded, carved grotto is roughly twelve feet high and just about as wide.
Poles of wood brace the walls, keeping them from caving in. There is no doubt
that this excavation project is unfinished and abandoned: mouldy ropes and wet,
broken tools lie scattered about the area, arranged in a way that leaves the
impression that the excavators left in a hurry. The burrow makes its way through
the moist, hard-packed earth to the north. To the south, a huge slab of black
stone blocks further passage.
name: Unfinished Troll Burrow

desc:
The earthy ground shifts in colours of dark brown and black, some parts softer
than others. The tunnel seems to have been hastily dug out, and cracked,
half-rotten wooden beams have been put up to support the irregular ceiling and
walls. A hole in the western wall leads into a shaft, while the tunnel itself
continues to the north and south.
name: Narrow Earth Tunnel

desc:
An irregularly-shaped hole in the ceiling, neither round nor square, opens into
a dark cave above. Small ledges remain from a recent excavation, creating easy
access to that higher tunnel. The eastern exit is lined with broken planks,
tilted boulders, and loose rocks, suggesting that a barrier was smashed to
pieces.
name: Narrow Shaft

desc:
This tunnel is but a dozen feet high and wide, and tapers off to the north. It
looks much like the tunnel of an exploring badger: round, with rough edges and
no apparent purpose. Beams of dark, rotted wood support the densely-packed, wet
soil walls and ceiling, keeping them from collapsing. The tunnel continues to
the south, where it widens slightly.
name: Narrow Earth Tunnel

desc:
There is a hole in the centre of this cavern floor, opening up into a steep
shaft. The shaft is lined with ledges every three to four feet, creating a crude
yet usable semi-natural staircase. The chute is deep, and its bottom must lie
too far down to be seen from this height. Broken planks, rusting pickaxes and
other tools lie spread about the cavern, seemingly abandoned. The cave ascends
to the north.
name: Precipitous Slope

desc:
This rock-choked tunnel continues to the north and south. Huge rocks and
boulders turn the steep slope into a maze, creating a terrain that is both
difficult and painful to navigate. The deep black walls and ceilings have been
crudely dug out with little skill and in obvious haste. A faint draft can be
felt from the north, bringing cold, dry air into the tunnel. Small spiders
scurry along the dirt-packed ground, disappearing into cracks and beneath rocks
when disturbed.
name: Precipitous Slope

desc:
The black rocks that make up the floor, ceiling and walls of this tunnel feels
dry and cold to the touch. A multitude of smaller rocks lie scattered across the
cavern floor, and the walls are uneven and jagged. It looks as if the tunnel was
excavated in haste and with little skill. The dark tunnel slopes steeply
downwards to the south, steeply enough that passage that way looks perilious. At
the top of the passageway, located to the north, a bigger cave can be discerned.
name: Precipitous Slope

desc:
Five tunnels converge here at this spacious intersection. To the south one
tunnel makes a steep descent, while the east and north offers wearying ascents.
A crude tunnel burrows deeper into the mountain to the west. Between the
southern and western tunnels a crack in the wall leads down towards a
crude-looking, descending staircase. The area is covered by a thick layer of
dust and dirt, imprinted with wide tracks leading off in all possible
directions. The ceiling is high and the cave is truly vast.
name: Five-way Crossing

desc:
The corridor ascends slightly from south to north. The ceiling arches overhead,
smooth and dome-shaped. Protruding edges and rocks stick out from the cavern
walls in a few places. The stone walls are black as night, and the air is cold
and damp. The dirty, dust-covered floor is marked by a number of footprints that
cross back and forth from south to north.
name: Pitch-black Corridor

desc:
An arched corridor extends from east to west. Green and grey moulds grow over
vast areas of the walls, covering large swaths of the wet, black bedrock.
Boulders and bigger rocks have been left in seemingly random places, most likely
remnants of the excavation process. Small, crumbling, dried-out husks from
insects litter the cavern floor along the walls, and spider webs stretch between
rocks and boulders.
name: Pitch-black Corridor

desc:
The dark stone walls and ceiling creates a dome that covers the entire length of
this corridor. Furhter passage is possible to the east and west. The walls are,
where not smooth, at least fairly even-textured. Traces of bat droppings line
the sides of the tunnel, and a decaying bat corpse lies covered with dust and
maggots next to a small boulder. A light, constant breeze of humid air blows
through the area.
name: Pitch-black Corridor

desc:
This dome-shaped, arched corridor is pitch-black in colour, and has been
excavated using crude methods. Sharp edges protrude at various points from the
walls, and some boulders and smaller rocks lie scattered throughout the hallway.
Footprints have been left all over the area, deeply imprinted into the thick
layer of dirt and dust on the ground. A light breeze blows through the corridor,
spreading a strong, rancid odour. The tunnel rises to the south, while to the
west it descends slightly.
name: Pitch-black Corridor

desc:
A dome-shaped tunnel comes to an end here in a rather narrow cavern. A lukewarm
breeze blows through the area, coming from the north and continuing through a
wide crack in the cavern's western wall. A narrow ledge just beneath the crack
gives easy access to it. A putrid odour envelops the cave, carried here by the
draft. A narrow, ascending stone tunnel works its way upwards through the large
crack in the western wall. The bedrock here is very dark and the walls are lined
with sharp, protruding edges. A carcass lies crushed under some boulders beneath
the narrow ledge.
name: Pitch-black Corridor

desc:
The tunnel narrows here, creating a short bottleneck. It widens again to the
east and west. On the western side a massive, round stone door lies cracked on
the ground, its hinges still hanging from the circular doorway. A massive hall
opens up beyond the broken entranceway. To the east the tunnel widens to a cave,
tall and spacious. Remainders of well-gnawed bones, rusted goblets and other
trinkets lie scattered on the ground here.
name: Crude Passageway

desc:
The caves open up here, going from tighter tunnels to spacious halls. Tall,
black pillars, crudely carved from the surrounding rocks support the vast
ceilings. In some areas, the pillars have been replaced by enormous, old,
withered logs. A long, centrally-located table rises from the floor, hewn
directly from the black stone that forms these caves. It is covered by the
remains of once-living creatures: long-dried entrails, cracked skulls, and
pulverized bones. The vast halls extend to the north and west. To the east a
cracked entranceway leads into a tapering tunnel.
name: Hewn Halls

desc:
The succession of big, roomy halls appear to end here. A chair of sorts has been
shaped from the stone that forms the northern wall. Its dark stone surface is
covered with dry soil and slimy sediment. The roof is supported by massive, hewn
tree trunks and pillars cut directly from the stone of the mountain. A bonfire
flickers with a fading light at the centre of the cave. The halls continue to
the south.
name: Hewn Halls

desc:
The ceiling here is quite high, and many shelves, carved directly into the hard,
black rock, line the walls. Pots, kettles, tools and barrels lie half-cracked,
half-crushed all over the cave. Smashed chests, rusted iron tools and moulding
foodstuffs lie scattered in the dirt. Rats, roaches and centipedes scurry along
fissures in the ground. To the south a wooden door is slowly rotting and falling
apart; it is the only visible exit out of here.
name: Abandoned Reserve

desc:
The stone stairs turn quickly, leading upwards to another level of the
underground caves. A rotting, skewed wooden frame outlines the tunnel to the
north. A small hallway of some sort is located to the west. A tightly-packed
layer of dirt covers the ground, with deep footprints leading in all directions.
name: Inclining Staircase

desc:
The stairs lead down, deeper into the dark mountain. The cave is crude, with
rough edges protruding from the walls. The unevenly-cut stairs are covered with
dust, rocks and random debris. Little bugs, roaches and spiders climb the walls
along the stairs. The dark, murky tunnel to the east appears passable.
name: Descending Staircase

desc:
A roughly-cut tunnel makes its way through the dark, cold mountain. Nothing
reflects from the poorly dug-out walls. Sharp, pointy edges protrude from all
surfaces. The ground is covered by a thin layer of dust and dirt. Several small
bat skeletons lie in one corner of the cave, and another has been crushed under
falling stones. East and west are staircases, and to the north the tunnel rises
into a slanting burrow.
name: Murky Tunnel

desc:
The ground is even, worn smooth from many decades of use. A shallow gutter has
been worn in the centre of the tunnel. The burrow rises fifteen or so feet tall,
with a ceiling of exposed, sharp, dark stone edges. The pathway runs up and
down, making it a strenuous route of travel. It extends further into darkness to
the east and south.
name: Slanting Burrow

desc:
A concave trail has been worn in the black stone underfoot, the result of heavy
use over many years. The burrow slopes down from the west and rises again to the
east, creating a small dip right here. To the north the cave opens up into a
deep chasm, the result of the burrow having been mined too deeply. Some twenty
feet across the deep pit is another ledge.
name: Slanting Burrow

desc:
A roughly-hewn staircase has been dug out of the deep, dark mountain. Its ascent
is steep, and it turns sharply to the northwest. The steps are quite high,
uneven, and worn-down. The exit to the west holds old hinges, set for a door;
the door frame has long since been shattered. At the bottom of the stairs lies a
stone door, broken into many pieces.
name: Stone Stairs

desc:
A ledge of black slate follows the southern wall of the cavern here. To the
north the architects of this cavern have dug far too deep, exposing a crevice
black as night, and with its bottom too far away to be visible. A similar ledge
as this one can be seen on the other side of the chasm, well out of reach to the
north. The burrow makes its way upwards, both to the east and west.
name: Slanting Burrow

desc:
Black, surprisingly fresh air rushes past your face as you plunge downwards,
deep, deep down towards the unfathomable depths of this broad crack in the
bedrock of the mountain. Were you not preoccupied with falling to your death,
you would notice that the rock walls appear to be of natural origin, with basalt
columns interspersed with clear mountain crystals and tourmalines.
name: Certain Death

desc:
Black, surprisingly fresh air rushes past your face as you plunge downwards,
deep, deep down towards the unfathomable depths of this broad crack in the
bedrock of the mountain. Were you not preoccupied with falling to your death,
you would notice that the rock walls appear to be of natural origin, with basalt
columns interspersed with clear mountain crystals and tourmalines.
name: Certain Death

desc:
A smooth pathway runs through the burrow, rising and falling with regularity.
The path has a concave shape to it, worn down in the middle after many years of
use. The black walls are rough, with sharp edges poking out here and there. A
small gust of air blows through the burrow every now and then.
name: Slanting Burrow

desc:
A small crack in the burrow's southern wall allows access to a staircase leading
down. The tunnels through the mountain here have low, rough ceilings, and crude
walls. Cockroaches and little bugs dart across the ground, aiming for the safety
of small cracks and holes in the rock. Low, slanting tunnels extend to the north
and west.
name: Confluence of Tunnels

desc:
This rounded tunnel, dug out from the black bedrock, ends southward at a steep
staircase. The tunnel is quite snug and cumbersome to travel. Bat droppings can
be seen here and there. A thin layer of dust covers most of the tunnel. The
accessway continues in a northernly direction.
name: Accessway

desc:
Three tunnels split apart here, with two of them slowly descending to the north
and south. The ceiling and floor slant from west to east, and a troll burrow
takes shape to the north. The black slate of the tunnel floor is solid
underfoot. The area appears to have been dug out solely for the purpose of
transport; and no embellishments or other niceties are present.
name: Accessway

desc:
It is clear this passage through the burrow has been in use for decades, as a
small concave trail has been worn down the middle of the tunnel by creatures
passing through. The cave is black stone, crudely dug out. Fragments from the
ceiling and walls lie scattered along the sides of the tunnel. The pathway
descends below, and rises slightly to the south.
name: Slanting Burrow

desc:
This narrow, winding tunnel makes its way through the black mountain, twisting
and turning through the bedrock. The ceiling and walls have a rounded shape to
them, and their surfaces are rough and black. The air is damp, and small pearls
of dew have condensed on the walls. Thick layers of bat droppings can be seen on
the ground. The tunnel continues in an easterly direction.
name: Accessway

desc:
A concave trail runs through the centre of the burrow, the hard black rock
underfoot worn down by time and use. The burrow slopes up and down, as if it
were dug without proper guidance. The pathway is quite arduous to traverse; in
addition to the steep slopes, there are rocks and boulders jutting out from the
walls, creating obstacles that nearly block some stretches of the tunnel. The
burrow continues east and west, and to the south abruptly rises and continues
upwards.
name: Slanting Burrow

desc:
A smooth, black rock ledge runs east to west along the northern wall of the
burrow. The cave complex has been mined too deeply to the south, and drops away
into a giant chasm, the bottom hidden in darkness. Another ledge can be seen to
the south, across the deep pit. Small webs stretch between sharp edges
protruding from the rough wall to the north, and some of the webs appear to have
entangled some of the small bugs that are ever-present in these caves.
name: Slanting Burrow

desc:
The burrow comes to an end here, in this foul, unpleasant dugout. The black rock
floor is covered with many broken, yellowed bones and dusty old tools. A small
bonfire lights the area, partially illuminating it with a dying, flickering
light. The crudely made burrow inclines slightly towars the east as it heads
deep into the mountain.
name: Slanting Burrow

desc:
The burrow floor rises sharply here, as if it were passing over an underground
hill. The black slate underfoot has been worn down, creating a concave trail
leading east and west. Heaps of bat guano cover some of the loose rocks
scattered about the area. The burrow walls are rounded, gradually curving
upwards to become the ceiling in an overhead arc.
name: Slanting Burrow

desc:
The dark burrow makes a north-west turn here, coming from the south. A putrid,
stingy smell spreads across the area, with a swift breeze coming in from the
west. The burrow slopes slightly to the west and south. The cave has been
reinforced with thick tree logs to keep the ceiling from caving in. The black
stone walls are cold and dry.
name: Bend in the Slanting Burrow

desc:
These dark mountain corridors have been mined into a tubular shape: the walls
and ceiling form a reasonably smooth arch. Some bigger rocks and boulders are
scattered throughout the corridor. The stone walls are very dark, the colour
shifting to green and deep purple in places where it is covered by thick sheafs
of mould. The air here is quite humid. The corridor continues both north and
south.
name: Pitch-black Corridor

desc:
The black stone walls of this place are cold and moist, and partially covered
with mould. Thick dust, small insects, spider webs and dried-out husks from bugs
cover much of the ground. Deep footprints cross through here, disappearing to
the east, where the ground becomes dust-free and nearly shining. The ground
slopes steeply, and it looks as if it is slowly being split in two by an
expanding crack in the rock.
name: Pitch-black Corridor

desc:
The tunnel widens as it descends, growing from a small crack above into the
large cavern it is here. Long stalactites hang from the ceiling; they are
massive, with sharp points, and resemble black icicles. Some have broken off and
fallen to the floor, where they lie in pieces. Natural pillars partially block
the view from any point in this cavern, but it is evident that this grand cave
stretches far to the north, east and south.
name: Bottom of a Tunnel

desc:
The ceiling varies in height here, rising far above the cave to the south, and
sloping steeply down to the north. Stalactites of various sizes hang overhead,
covering the majority of the ceiling. A hole in the ground can be seen in the
far north corner of this cave, out of which a sparse cloud of fumes rises. To
the south the cave expands, forming a huge space. Black, moist stone pillars
stand close to the walls, and water is dripping down their sides.
name: End of a Tunnel

desc:
This cave is tall and expansive. Stalactites hang from the ceiling and
stalagmites rise from the floor; in places these have met, forming pillars that
look worn-away about halfway between ceiling and floor. The air is heavy and
moist. Large portions of the dewy cave have been covered by frothy mould. The
black of the surrounding stone shifts into the blue-green of the mould where
this has occurred. The vast cave expands to the south and west.
name: Tenebrous Cavern

desc:
This cave has an odd shimmer to it, with colours shifting from the deepest black
of the surrounding stone to the green-blue of the mould growing on the walls. A
thin, cold mist engulfs the area, carrying a strong odour with it. Condensation
clings to the walls, and stalagmites of various sizes rise from the floor. Old,
cracked skulls and crushed bones lie scattered among the conical calcium
deposits. The vast cave expands further into the shadows to the north and east.
name: Tenebrous Cavern

desc:
Long stalactites and tall stalagmites line the edges of this cavern. The air is
very damp, and a layer of condensation covers the black slate ground. Bugs dart
across the floor, running from fissure to fissure. The odour of decaying flesh
completely fills the area. This giant, deep cave expands further to the north
and west.
name: Tenebrous Cavern

desc:
A black, putrid pond located in the centre of this crudely-mined cave seems to
be the source of the harsh fumes that cloud the air. A rickety wooden staircase
leans against the eastern wall, leading up to a dark cave. The tunnel, dug out
from soft, brown soil, is supported by thick wooden beams and black stone
boulders. It continues in a northernly direction. The area is quite cramped, and
the air is lukewarm and damp.
name: Rancid Pond

desc:
Reinforced by logs and stone blocks, this creaking tunnel makes its way from
south to north. The ceiling is uneven, and small pebbles and chunks of dirt have
fallen from above in many places. The ground is soft, almost wet. Small droplets
of water trickle down the slowly-rotting wooden beams that support the walls and
ceiling. Clouds of thick, mist-like fumes hang like putrid-smelling drapes in
the air.
name: Rough Earth Tunnel

desc:
The tunnel slants slightly here as it slopes downwards from north to south.
Small centipedes and other bugs scurry along the wet, dark-brown dirt walls. The
logs keeping the tunnel from collapsing are slowly rotting, and are
partially-covered by a green-white mould. Debris covers most of the ground:
decaying wooden splinters and partially-burned rope have been trampled deeply
into the sodden dirt floor.
name: Humid Earth Tunnel

desc:
The ground is covered by a thick layer of grey-white dust mixed with brown dirt.
Decomposing, half-eaten bodies have been placed throughout the vaulted crypt. A
hole in the floor in the north-east corner of the crypt opens up into a dank
earth tunnel. The walls here have been hung with femoral and humeral bones as
well as crania, suggestive of a ghastly trophy room. The troll-made burrows
continue into similar-sized rooms to the south and west.
name: Faltering Troll Lair

desc:
The area is absolutely crowded with broken bones, skulls, rags, splintered
tools, and rusted blades. Everything lies in differently-sized piles, in
complete disarray. It is suggestive of a mass tomb. Cockroaches and black-scaled
bugs scurry among the skeletal remains. The ceiling is quite high, and vaults
have been shaped between this cave and neighbouring caves to the north and west.
The walls are lined with skulls; gaping holes have been punched through their
crania, and their eye sockets are thick with spider webs. A narrow chute has
been dug through the eastern wall.
name: Faltering Troll Burrow

desc:
A large stone table has been set in the centre of the room. Wooden stools and
chairs were once here as well, but they have been smashed, their splintered
remains spread across the floor. Broken skeletons and armour line the walls.
Part of the vaults separating the crypts are slowly collapsing, and a number of
thickstone blocks lie on the ground beneath them. Several other lairs and
burrows can be explored to the east and south.
name: Faltering Troll Lair

desc:
This lair is filled with crushed rib bones, broken skulls, and rotting wooden
tools. Small, quick bugs dart from crack to crack as they make their way across
the floor. A massive boar corpse is rotting away in one corner, its head
half-eaten and its ribcage completely exposed. The ceiling is rounded, with
small arches separating this place from the lairs to the east and north. To the
west, rocks, stones and broken logs have collapsed into a huge pile, which is
covered with a thick layer of dust. Space is quite limited here.
name: Faltering Troll Lair

desc:
A smooth, rounded chute makes a steep ascent up to the eastern wall, then
quickly turns northwest. The perfectly circular shape of the chute and the
smoothness of the black stone hint of the chute's frequent use as a conveying
passage. Deep tracks run along the walls and ground, following the direction of
the tunnel. The ceiling is lower compared to the neighbouring caves, and a brisk
gust of wind blows through at irregular intervals. To the west the caves expand
further into the darkness.
name: Narrow Chute

desc:
A big, gaping crack has opened in the centre of the ceiling. On the ground along
the walls lie huge fallen rocks and boulders. Skeletons, crafting tools,
barrels, and rusted weapons have nearly disintegrated beneath the rockfall. A
thick layer of dust engulfs the ruined crypt. The air is heavy, saturated with
ashes and grit. The rubble is arduous to navigate through; there is little space
in which to move. Massive beams of wood have collapsed under the weight of the
mountain, with splinters spread far across the room. A tiny hole can be seen to
the south, between two massive, steadfast boulders. To the east some sort of
troll-made chamber has been dug out of the rubble.
name: Shattered Troll-chamber

desc:
A low-cut cave, with rough ceilings and walls, opens up here. A tunnel leads
downwards: it appears to be dark and cramped, and it quickly turns in a
westernly direction. Flakes of stone are coming off the walls, gathering in
small piles of debris on the ground. A fungus-like, putrid smell chokes the
heavy, humid air. Cockroaches are ever-present on the walls and ground, swiftly
darting into small cracks and holes when disturbed.
name: Dark Grotto

desc:
The damp, cold air that settles heavily here is thick with the distinct scents
of mould and decay. Rough walls and an uneven ceiling form the boundaries of
this grotto which is littered with cracked skulls, discarded foodstuffs and
random debris; all of which have all been swept into the corners. There is an
arch in the northern end of the cave, but no visible passageway: it ends in
another wall. To the west a dark, dust-filled cave can be seen.
name: Dark Grotto

desc:
The rough, low ceiling in here gives off the impression that this is a smaller
cavern than it actually is. To the west a big crack has broken the ceiling and
the walls, leaving a sharp ledge approximately fifteen feet up. Pebbles and
smaller rocks are slowly piling up here. To the east a dark grotto can be seen.
name: Riven Cavern

desc:
A greasy layer of thick, strong-smelling grime covers the roughly-cut walls of
this cavern. The cavern is quite cramped, with large boulders and rocks lining
the walls. Black scales lie crushed on these boulders, and also on the ground.
The air is musty, lukewarm and heavy. A wooden trough of some kind has been
split in two, its broken pieces lying in the centre of the grotto. To the east
another rough-smelling cave can be discerned.
name: Dark Grotto

desc:
This narrow, winding crawlspace is the result of a recent earthquake. Massive
boulders mixed with smaller rocks has crashed down to block what was formerly a
wide tunnel. Wooden beams and sharp rocks point out in all directions, making it
difficult for even the smallest of creatures to make any headway. Only this tiny
passage remains, and it is so small that only a hobbit could possibly crawl
through it.
name: Narrow Crawlspace

desc:
A tiny pocket of air has been created in the aftermath of the cave-in. Large
beams of broken wood lie criss-crossed in the small space, leaving enough
leverage and support to keep the ceiling from collapsing further. There are
several troll-like limbs and bodyparts crushed underneath the black, sharp
rocks. The dust is dense in the air, and the lukewarm temperature creates a
perfect atmosphere for mould, larvae, and worms to infest the decaying bodies.
The stench is beyond putrid. A narrow gap through the black mountain rocks can
be seen to the east. A tiny hole lined by razor-sharp rocks opens up into a
large, vast cavern to the south.
name: Narrow Crawlspace

desc:
A giant crack opens up here, far inside the mountain. The height of the fissure
indicates the true depth of these caves, and gazing upwards one can see massive
black stalactites hanging down from the high ceiling. Coarse stone, black as
night, forms the surfaces of the walls. The floor is covered by a layer of black
grit, criss-crossed with large footprints. Broken, twisted skeletons, completely
stripped of all soft tissues, lie tossed aside into the corners. The place is
massive, and stretches further east and south. To the north a cave-in has
occurred, leaving no discernible exits.
name: Heart of the Mountain

desc:
An old stone table sits cracked in the centre of the cave. Wiped clean of any
foodstuffs, only mould and fungi cover it now. A skeleton the size of a
man-child lies broken in several pieces in a corner of the cave. It has been
completely picked clean of any soft tissue. Trickles of dirt and pebbles have
landed in piles across the expanse of the cave - clear evidence of recent,
ongoing seismic activities. An enormous cave opens up to the north, and the
cavern also expands further to the east.
name: Ruined Troll-Hole

desc:
This is a dank, dirt-covered cave, nestled deep among the very roots of the
mountain. Thick air, polluted by black dust and a ghastly smell permeates the
black cavern. Fragments of bone lie scattered across the room, mixed together
with various bits of wooden and metal debris. The entire area appears to be
sealed off with no obvious exits out to any sort of tunnel or escape route.
Small stalactites hang from the ceiling, and tiny drops of water are slowly
rippling down their sides.
name: Ruined Troll-Hole

desc:
The cavern is tall and wide, and the walls, ceiling and ground are dark as
night. A layer of dust covers most of the area. Smashed barrels and chests lie
scattered all over. Small rocks and pebbles tumble down the walls at irregular
intervals, and piles of rubble are slowly growing beneath the most active of
these rockfalls. The cave turns in a south-to-west direction, creating a
centrally-located natural pillar around which the immediate caves have been dug.
There are no apparent exits away from this litter-strewn, forsaken area.
name: Ruined Troll-Hole

desc:
A huge black portal, forged from seven massive stone blocks tethered together by
iron bars and rusted bolts, blocks the northern exit from the cave. A row of
four thick, oxidized iron rings hangs from the gate. The cavern itself is both
wide and tall, with sharp edges of black stone protruding from the ceiling and
walls. Shards of shattered stone lie spread across the ground. Remnants of
man-like bodies have been left here, rotting away in the lukewarmth. In the
southeastern corner a tunnel accessway takes a sharp turn, leading further down
into the depths of Ettenmoors.
name: Before a Great Portal
